acts.ui.stats_text: {ev} events ({secs} sections + {subs} sub-events); {par} have New Testament parallels and {none} have none (all of them section rows). {tagged} numbered places from the 38 maps are attached to event rows, and {ndiff} events carry a note on how they differ from the Bible.
acts.guide.1: This book follows the life of Jesus in the order of The Urantia Book and shows, at a glance, which New Testament passages correspond to each event. It is based on Dr. William S. Sadler’s comparative study “Jesus in the New Testament and The Urantia Book.” Event names and section titles follow the text of The Urantia Book.
acts.guide.2: Each table has three columns: Event / Urantia Book / Bible. A bold row is a section of The Urantia Book; rows beginning with “·” beneath it are sub-events within that section that have their own Bible parallels. A row marked “(Introduction)” or without a number is the opening of the paper (section 0). The Urantia Book column gives paper:section.paragraph; a section row gives its first to last paragraph, a sub-event row the paragraph(s) where it is told. Every reference was checked against the text.
acts.guide.3: The Bible column gives the corresponding New Testament passages (Matt., Mark, Luke, John, Acts). Where there is no parallel, the column reads “None.” Where the source gives no passage for a section but its sub-events have one, the sub-event passages are also gathered on the section row.
acts.guide.4: Under each event a short paragraph describes what happens, drawn from the text of The Urantia Book. Where the Bible has a parallel and the two accounts actually differ — in persons, places, timing, order, the nature of a miracle, or the words spoken — a note in red, “Differs from the Bible,” is added. Where there is no clear difference, no note is given.
acts.guide.5: The gray text beside each paper title is the approximate time (year and month) of its events, following the years given in the section titles and the dates in the text; where a date is not stated it is estimated from the surrounding events. Papers that contain only teaching or commentary carry no date.
acts.guide.6: How the maps are combined: the 38 maps of Jesus’ journeys (each with numbered places) are woven into the tables. (1) A blue band marks where each map begins: “Map number · title · period.” (2) Each numbered place is attached to the event row that contains the first paragraph it cites (small text under the event name, e.g., “Map 20-④ By boat to Kheresa”). (3) The map itself is printed just below the table of the paper in which its band appears, and its numbered notes are set beneath the map in readable type. Place locations are approximate, positions within cities are schematic, and the base terrain is from Natural Earth (public domain). The Map Index at the end lists every place and the paragraph it cites.
acts.appx.1: Passages of the New Testament that the source study notes are not found in The Urantia Book.
acts.appx.2: The 38 maps of Jesus’ journeys and their numbered places. The right column gives the paragraphs each place cites; in the tables the place is attached to the event row containing the first of them.
acts.fix.1: Obvious slips in the source study were corrected: “Mark 1:1-60” at 135:6 → Mark 1:1-8; “Matt. 5:14-15” for Peter’s mother-in-law → Matt. 8:14-15; “John 19:9-42” at 188:1 → John 19:39-42; colon slips such as “Luke 8:1:3”; and Paper 157, sections 5–7, which the source labels as Paper 158.
acts.fix.2: Where the source only says “see section 8” or “see section 3” (150:9 and 164:4), the passages are given, and John 9 is divided between 164:3 (John 9:1-12) and 164:4 (John 9:13-41).
acts.fix.3: Passages were supplied, after checking the text, where the source gives none: 140:4 (Matt. 5:13-16), 140:5 (the beatitudes, Matt. 5:3-12; Luke 6:20-23), and 169:1 (the prodigal son, Luke 15:11-32).
acts.fix.4: The farewell discourse, which the source groups as “John 14:1–16:28,” is divided section by section (180:2–6).
acts.fix.5: The source says Luke 2:21 (the circumcision) is not in The Urantia Book, but 122:8.2 says Jesus “was circumcised on the eighth day,” so it is listed as a sub-event.
acts.fix.6: At 147:2 the source also lists John 15 and 16, which do not fit the narrative; they are omitted, and the pool of Bethesda (John 5) is placed at 147:3.
